Scenario_Summary: Published full-text methods report a named formal hypothesis test, test statistic, and p-value linked to compared forecasting methods.
Author_Comments: Explicitly reported hypothesis testing with a test statistic and p-value satisfies the YES evidence threshold.

Scenario_Summary: Full text explicitly states simulated trades assumed zero transaction fees.
Author_Comments: The explicit assumption of zero transaction fees supports EXPLICIT_NO for transaction-cost inclusion.

Scenario_Summary: Accessible full text and linked available supplementary methods searched for statistical tests; none documented.
Author_Comments: Documented searching of accessible full text and supplements without finding statistical testing supports NOT_REPORTED, not confirmed non-performance.

Scenario_Summary: Methods say the evaluation was chronological while experiment description describes shuffled samples; temporal ordering cannot be resolved.
Author_Comments: Contradictory descriptions of chronological and shuffled evaluation justify AMBIGUOUS until the conflict is resolved.

Scenario_Summary: Preprocessing timing is specified only in a cited appendix that could not be retrieved; accessible main paper does not resolve the field.
Author_Comments: The unavailable appendix prevents verification of preprocessing timing; INSUFFICIENT_ACCESS is appropriate.

Scenario_Summary: Abstract explicitly names a paired performance test, reports p-value and identifies the forecasting-model comparison.
Author_Comments: The abstract provides explicit, identifiable statistical-test evidence sufficient for YES, with the abstract recorded as the source.

Scenario_Summary: Only abstract accessible; it reports an 80/20 split but does not establish chronological order.
Author_Comments: An 80/20 split does not establish chronological validation. Limited source access justifies INSUFFICIENT_ACCESS.

Scenario_Summary: Only title, year and DOI available; no source evidence of trading/economic evaluation.
Author_Comments: Bibliographic metadata alone cannot establish economic evaluation; INSUFFICIENT_ACCESS is appropriate.

Scenario_Summary: Study only predicts numerical prices and explicitly performs no trading or decision backtest: transaction-cost criterion is inapplicable.
Author_Comments: Transaction-cost evaluation is NOT_APPLICABLE because the study contains no trading or decision backtest.

Scenario_Summary: Primary forecasting experiment shows positive safeguards on all applicable material pathways, but a separate secondary experiment has verified leakage.
Author_Comments: Accepted with clarification. The primary forecasting experiment may be classified as LOW leakage risk only when all applicable safeguards are positively verified. The secondary experiment with confirmed leakage must retain a separate HIGH-risk classification. Both experiment-level assessments must be preserved, and the study must not be described as universally leakage-free.

Scenario_Summary: Paper reports a code repository URL, but archive and repository cannot be accessed on verification date; no authenticated code obtained.
Author_Comments: Accepted with clarification. Reporting a repository URL confirms that a code link was provided but does not establish verified public code accessibility. Repository-link reporting and authenticated code availability must be recorded separately. When the repository cannot be accessed, code availability remains unverified, with the access attempt and verification date documented.

Scenario_Summary: Attempt to aggregate ordinal leakage-risk judgment into the generic YES/NO four-column publication crosswalk must be rejected.
Author_Comments: Ordinal leakage-risk categories must remain separate from the binary evidence-state reporting crosswalk.
